additions.reason: The mochin are the four supernal intellects (חכמה, בינה, חסד, גבורה) that are clothed in נצח-הוד-יסוד of Binah. They are the central node of Package 1 — the supernal lights that bless Ze'ir Anpin and flow down to build Malkhut. The text says 'הַמֹּחִין הֵם אַרְבַּע: חָכְמָה בִּינָה חֶסֶד וּגְבוּרָה, וְהֵם מְלֻבָּשִׁים בְּנֶצַח-הוֹד-יְסוֹד דְּבִינָה. וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת: כְּאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים'.
additions.source_quote: וְהַמֹּחִין הֵם אַרְבַּע: חָכְמָה בִּינָה חֶסֶד וּגְבוּרָה, וְהֵם מְלֻבָּשִׁים בְּנֶצַח-הוֹד-יְסוֹד דְּבִינָה. וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת: כְּאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים

additions.reason: The primordial light of the seven days is explicitly named as the bechina-equivalent of the four mochin clothed in Binah's netzach-hod-yesod. It is also identified as the secret of the two forms of shin. This is the central pivot concept in Package 1, connecting the mochin cluster to the letter-shin cluster.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת: כְּאוֹר שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים, שֶׁהֵם סוֹד שִׁין שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁין וְשִׁין שֶׁל אַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁין

additions.reason: The standard three-headed shin (ש) is the sod (secret) of the light of the seven days. Together with its four-headed counterpart it constitutes the bechina-equivalent of the mochin/primordial light. The three heads correspond to three of the four mochin (Chokhmah-Binah-Chesed or a similar grouping in the Arizal's system).
additions.source_quote: שֶׁהֵם סוֹד שִׁין שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁין וְשִׁין שֶׁל אַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁין

additions.reason: The four-headed shin (found in tefillin shel rosh) is also the sod of the primordial light of the seven days, corresponding to the fourth of the four mochin (Gevurah). Together with the three-headed shin it represents the totality of the four mochin as expressed in the form of the letter shin.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁהֵם סוֹד שִׁין שֶׁל שְׁלֹשָׁה רָאשִׁין וְשִׁין שֶׁל אַרְבָּעָה רָאשִׁין

additions.reason: The netzach-hod-yesod of Binah are the vessels in which the four mochin are clothed before they pass into Ze'ir Anpin. They are thus bechina-equivalent to the mochin in their clothed form — they share the same essential reality of being the transmission channel for supernal intellectual light.

Malkhut is the central concept of Package 2. The text presents it in its initial state בִּבְחִינַת 'אוֹשִׁיט פְּסִיעָה לְבַר' — extending one small step outside Ze'ir Anpin. This is holy Malkhut in its katnut (diminished) state before receiving mochin. The whole Torah is about how to fix (לְתַקְּנָהּ) and grow (וּלְגַדְּלָהּ) this Malkhut.
additions.source_quote: מִתְּחִלָּה הַמַּלְכוּת הִיא אֵצֶל זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין, בִּבְחִינַת אוֹשִׁיט פְּסִיעָה לְבַר

additions.reason: This Zohar phrase (from Parshat Balak, folio 203b) describes the initial state of Malkhut — extending only a small step outward. The text uses it explicitly as a bechina description of Malkhut's starting condition: 'בִּבְחִינַת אוֹשִׁיט פְּסִיעָה לְבַר'. It is a neutral concept: neither evil nor fully good, but the intermediate, constricted state of Malkhut before it is elevated.
additions.source_quote: בִּבְחִינַת אוֹשִׁיט פְּסִיעָה לְבַר, כַּמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
